**Astra agent review — AI-generated, not manually written by the maintainer.**

The new host method is missing from the published TypeScript contract. I checked the current declarations with tsc and exercised the exact-head WorldRenderer with real THREE 0.128.0; eight focused host/texture tests pass. No browser/GL test was run.

Skills used: prismarine-architecture-review helped trace the host extension contract through its exported declarations; prismarine-behavior-test-review guided the focused type/runtime checks; prismarine-review helped verify the current head and absence of duplicate feedback.

**Astra agent review — AI-generated, not manually written by the maintainer.**

One additional dependency-compatibility regression is inline. Validation: real 1.20.4 protocol client/server comparison against the current head and its actual base physics plugin, with the same installed dependencies; the head fails and the base passes. The existing focused 1.21.4 physics tests pass. No vanilla server suite was run.

Skills used: prismarine-protocol-data-review checked the declared dependency range and feature availability; prismarine-behavior-test-review guided the observable regression test; prismarine-review prevented duplicating the existing lifecycle finding.

**Astra agent review — AI-generated, not manually written by the maintainer.**

Rechecked the current head and all discussion and found one distinct dropped-item fallback regression after a known stack's texture lookup. Reproduced with the actual base/current rendering methods, Three.js 0.128.0 and the released minecraft-assets 1.17.0 index; image-loader callbacks and animation were controlled, and no WebGL or live server was run. The existing pending-stack and disposal comments were not repeated.

Skills used: prismarine-behavior-test-review established the observable geometry regression; prismarine-architecture-review traced item-group ownership after lookup; prismarine-review checked current revisions and avoided duplicate feedback.

**Astra agent review — AI-generated, not manually written by the maintainer.**

I found one additional completion-boundary issue after comparing the current diff and all prior feedback. The current-head controller with released prismarine-physics 1.11.1 reaches a one-step goal but rejects when blocks is 1. This was a local simulation on a flat full-cube floor; I did not run the server suite.

Skills used: prismarine-behavior-test-review helped check the observable completion result at the step limit; prismarine-review helped distinguish it from the existing cancellation and tick-deadline findings.

**Astra agent review — AI-generated, not manually written by the maintainer.**

I found a separate fluid-path gap in the flight handling. All five added test bodies passed in a small assertion-adapter runner; an idle flying player still sank in water and lava using real 1.13.2 and 1.20.4 block data and this head's simulator. I also checked the vanilla Player/LivingEntity fluid gate and travel wrapper in the 1.20.3-pre1 source. No live vanilla server or full suite was run.

Skills used: prismarine-behavior-test-review helped compare idle hover across actual block environments; prismarine-architecture-review helped trace the flight mode through the shared movement branches; prismarine-review helped avoid repeating the existing jump/sneak finding.

**Astra agent review — AI-generated, not manually written by the maintainer.**

I checked the current handshake changes and public declarations, ran the 40 focused handshake tests successfully, and reproduced the TypeScript errors below against this head. The existing cookie-schema limitation is already documented and is not repeated here. No vanilla server or full suite was run.

Skills used: prismarine-code-quality-review helped check the documented public API against its declarations; prismarine-review helped verify the current head and avoid duplicate feedback.

**Astra agent review — AI-generated, not manually written by the maintainer.**

Re-reviewed head 27805567aa88bbc140c5b3d91766fe8a47fd105b and current discussion. All nine existing raycast tests pass; a focused stationary bottom-slab reproduction shows a visible top face rejected by strict mode. No vanilla server was run.

Skills used: prismarine-behavior-test-review guided validation against the real world/chunk geometry; prismarine-review helped identify the separate root cause and avoid repeating prior feedback.

**Astra agent review — AI-generated, not manually written by the maintainer.**

One new finding on the effective interaction ranges. I checked the production entity handler and actual NMP encoders/decoders on 1.21.1 and 1.21.4, using minecraft-protocol 1.67.0 and minecraft-data 3.114.0, and traced vanilla's attribute packet, final clamping and reach getters. This was an in-process codec/plugin reproduction, not a live-server test.

Skills used: prismarine-protocol-data-review helped distinguish the transmitted base/modifiers from the effective attribute; prismarine-behavior-test-review helped exercise the public reach predicates; prismarine-review helped separate this defect from the existing ownership and test-quality feedback.
